reason: Section 26 gives each spouse equal possession rights in household goods subject to orders and domestic contracts, and states when the right ends.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Spouses equal possession rights in household goods
proposedGroups.reason: Section 26 gives each spouse equal possession rights in household goods subject to orders and domestic contracts, and states when the right ends.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the equal possession right in household goods and when it terminates.

reason: Section 27 has distinct household goods topics: application, pending-disposal restriction, order powers, and exercise-of-power considerations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application for household goods order
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 27(1) allows a spouse to apply for an order respecting specified household goods not already covered by an exclusive possession order.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a spouse may apply for a household goods order.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Restriction on disposition while application pending
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 27(2) bars the other spouse from disposing of specified household goods while the application is pending without consent or leave.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the restriction on disposing of household goods after notice of an application.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Exclusive possession and non-disposition orders for household goods
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 27(3) allows exclusive possession and non-disposition orders with incidental, supplemental, and consequential provisions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the orders the Court may make for household goods after an application.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Considerations for household goods orders
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 27(4) directs the Court to consider daily-life needs, family responsibilities, and all other circumstances.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the considerations for exercising household goods order powers.

reason: Section 28 states when subsection 27(3) orders terminate and when the Court may vary, discharge, or suspend them.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Termination or variation of household goods orders
proposedGroups.reason: Section 28 states when subsection 27(3) orders terminate and when the Court may vary, discharge, or suspend them.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when household goods orders terminate and when they may be varied, discharged, or suspended.

reason: Section 29 separates compensation for wrongful disposition of household goods, notice-based limits, and double-recovery prevention.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Payment for loss of household goods use and enjoyment
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 29(1) allows a fair and reasonable payment order when specified household goods were disposed of without consent and the Court would have made a household goods order.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Court may order payment for loss of use and enjoyment of household goods.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No order against value good faith no-notice acquirer
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 29(2) prevents orders against persons who acquired for value, in good faith, and without notice.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the protection for a person acquiring household goods for value, in good faith, and without notice.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No further order after payment or satisfaction
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 29(3) prevents another order under the section after payment or satisfaction of an order.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how section 29 prevents repeated payment orders for the same household goods.

reason: Section 30 allows registration, renewal, discharge, amendment, and cancellation of notice of household goods orders and deems registration to be notice.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration and notice effect of household goods orders
proposedGroups.reason: Section 30 allows registration, renewal, discharge, amendment, and cancellation of notice of household goods orders and deems registration to be notice.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how notices of household goods orders are registered and how registration affects notice.

reason: Section 31 directs the Court to consider all circumstances, including expenditures caused by loss of use and replacement household goods.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Circumstances for wrongful household goods payment
proposedGroups.reason: Section 31 directs the Court to consider all circumstances, including expenditures caused by loss of use and replacement household goods.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the circumstances the Court considers when exercising section 29 powers and setting payment amounts.

reason: Section 32 limits the effect of non-possessory sales or security interests in household goods unless the spouse consents and joins the instrument.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Effect of sale or security interest in household goods without consent

evidenceText: Effect of sale or the giving of a security interest in household goods without consent of spouse

proposedGroups.reason: Section 32 limits the effect of non-possessory sales or security interests in household goods unless the spouse consents and joins the instrument.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a sale or security interest in household goods conveys no right, title, or interest without spousal consent.

reason: Section 33 defines domestic contract, marriage contract, and separation agreement for Part 3.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Domestic contract definitions
proposedGroups.reason: Section 33 defines domestic contract, marriage contract, and separation agreement for Part 3.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Part 3 definitions of domestic contract, marriage contract, and separation agreement.

reason: Section 34 authorizes marriage contracts about rights and obligations while barring agreement on parenting time or decision-making responsibility.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Marriage contract scope and parenting limits
proposedGroups.reason: Section 34 authorizes marriage contracts about rights and obligations while barring agreement on parenting time or decision-making responsibility.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what may be included in a marriage contract and what parenting matters may not be agreed to.

reason: Section 35 authorizes agreements between unmarried cohabitants, bars parenting-time and decision-making terms, and deems the agreement a marriage contract if the parties later marry.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Domestic contract for unmarried cohabitants
proposedGroups.reason: Section 35 authorizes agreements between unmarried cohabitants, bars parenting-time and decision-making terms, and deems the agreement a marriage contract if the parties later marry.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the scope, parenting limits, and later-marriage effect of a domestic contract between cohabitants.

reason: Section 36 authorizes separation agreements between persons living separate and apart or agreeing to do so, including property, support, parenting, and other settlement matters.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Separation agreement scope
proposedGroups.reason: Section 36 authorizes separation agreements between persons living separate and apart or agreeing to do so, including property, support, parenting, and other settlement matters.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may enter a separation agreement and what matters it may cover.

reason: Section 37 requires domestic contracts and amendments or rescissions to be in writing, signed, and witnessed.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Execution requirements for domestic contracts
proposedGroups.reason: Section 37 requires domestic contracts and amendments or rescissions to be in writing, signed, and witnessed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the writing, signature, and witnessing requirements for domestic contracts.

reason: Section 38 states when minors and representatives may enter domestic contracts or give waivers and consents.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Capacity to contract and representative authority
proposedGroups.reason: Section 38 states when minors and representatives may enter domestic contracts or give waivers and consents.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the capacity and representative-approval rules for domestic contracts, waivers, and consents.

reason: Section 39 allows the Court to disregard domestic contract provisions on child support, parenting time, or decision-making responsibility if doing so is in the child's best interests.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Best interests override for child matters
proposedGroups.reason: Section 39 allows the Court to disregard domestic contract provisions on child support, parenting time, or decision-making responsibility if doing so is in the child's best interests.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Court may disregard child-related domestic contract provisions.

reason: Section 40 makes certain chastity-dependent rights void while preserving pre-1981 separation agreement provisions as remarriage or cohabitation contingencies.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Chastity provisions in domestic contracts
proposedGroups.reason: Section 40 makes certain chastity-dependent rights void while preserving pre-1981 separation agreement provisions as remarriage or cohabitation contingencies.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the effect of chastity provisions in separation agreements and marriage contracts.

reason: Section 41 deems certain pre-1981 separation agreements and marriage contracts domestic contracts and validates contracts made before commencement in contemplation of the Part.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Transitional domestic contract provisions
proposedGroups.reason: Section 41 deems certain pre-1981 separation agreements and marriage contracts domestic contracts and validates contracts made before commencement in contemplation of the Part.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how pre-1981 agreements are treated as domestic contracts.

reason: Section 42 states that domestic contracts prevail over conflicting provisions of the Act, subject to sections 39 and 43.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Domestic contract paramountcy
proposedGroups.reason: Section 42 states that domestic contracts prevail over conflicting provisions of the Act, subject to sections 39 and 43.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a domestic contract prevails over the Act.

reason: Section 43 allows the Court to disregard domestic contract provisions when applying them would be inequitable and specified pre-1981 or independent-legal-advice conditions exist.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court disregard of inequitable domestic contract provisions

evidenceText: Court may disregard provision of domestic contract

proposedGroups.reason: Section 43 allows the Court to disregard domestic contract provisions when applying them would be inequitable and specified pre-1981 or independent-legal-advice conditions exist.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Court may disregard a domestic contract provision as inequitable.
